<strong>Date of Birth:</strong> May 18, 2006</p>

<hr />
<h3 style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Before UNH</strong></h3>

<p style="text-align: justify;">Mady Harvey competes on Beam, Vault, and Bars. She trained under <strong>George Young</strong> at <strong>Mid Michigan Gymnastics</strong>, where she developed strong fundamentals and competitive consistency. Known for her precision and poise, Mady brings energy and determination to every routine.</p>

<hr />
<h3 style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Academic & Personal Highlights</strong></h3>

<p style="text-align: justify;">Mady graduated from <strong>Freeland High School</strong>, home of the Falcons, where she ranked <strong>5th in her class of 130</strong> and was a member of the <strong>National Honor Society</strong>. She is majoring in <strong>Exercise Science</strong> and aspires to become a <strong>Sports Medicine Doctor</strong>, combining her passion for athletics and health care.</p>

<hr />
<h3 style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Family & Background</strong></h3>

<p style="text-align: justify;">Mady comes from an athletic family—her sister <strong>Ally Harvey</strong> plays soccer at Alma College, and her other sister, <strong>Ashley</strong>, is 23. Growing up in Freeland, Michigan, Mady developed a love for sports and outdoor activities that continues today.</p>

	<li style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Favorite TV Show:</strong> <em>How I Met Your Mother</em></li>
	<li style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Instagram:</strong> @harveymadison06</li>

style=\"text-align: justify;\">\u003Cspan style=\"font-size:14px;\">\u003Cstrong>Lindsey Bruck Ayotte\u003C/strong> is in her seventh season as head coach of the UNH gymnastics program in 2025-26.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2025, the UNH gymnastics team placed 51\u003Csup>st\u003C/sup> nationally with a 195.005 NQS. The Wildcats closed the season with their three highest scores of the season in their final three meets: 195.525 at Nebraska (March 8), 195.750 versus Rutgers (March 16), and a third-place 195.700 at the EAGL Championship (March 22), which was just 0.25 points away from winning the league crown. Junior \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/sports/womens-gymnastics/roster/serena-mullin/11335\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"11335\">Serena Mullin\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Hamden, Conn.) was named Team MVP after a season in which she was named All-EAGL First Team on balance beam and all-around and All-EAGL Second Team on floor exercise. Sophomore \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/sports/womens-gymnastics/roster/anne-challman/11329\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"11329\">Anne Challman\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Lewisburg, Pa.) and freshman \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/sports/womens-gymnastics/roster/aine-reade/11342\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"11342\">Aine Reade\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Merrimac, Mass.) were each selected to compete as floor exercise specialists in the NCAA Alabama Gymnastics Regional Championship. Reade, an eight-time EAGL Rookie of the Week, ranked No. 3 on floor in EAGL's regular season with a 9.865 NQS. Led by four-time honoree \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/sports/womens-gymnastics/roster/gracy-mowers/11334\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"11334\">Gracy Mowers\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Middleton, Mass.), all 18 members of the team were named to the EAGL All-Scholastic Team.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nUnder Bruck Ayotte's leadership in 2024, grad student \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/sports/womens-gymnastics/roster/kylie-gorgenyi/10265\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"10265\">Kylie Gorgenyi\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (North Reading, Mass.), a four-time NCAA Championship competitor, became the fourth Wildcat, and the first since \u003Cstrong>Meghan Pflieger\u003C/strong> in 2015, to win the EAGL Gymnast of the Year award. The four-time EAGL All-Scholastic Team honoree registered a career-high 9.950 on floor (March 17, tied for fourth in school history) and posted a PB 39.475 in all-around (Feb. 25) that tied UNH's highest score ever (\u003Cstrong>Amanda Hall\u003C/strong>, March 6, 2004). The 'Cats scored a season-high 196.150, its highest EAGL Championship score in six years, and placed runner-up to host and back-to-back league champion Towson in the 2024 EAGL Championship.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2023, senior co-captain \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/sports/womens-gymnastics/roster/robyn-kelley/9481\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"9481\">Robyn Kelley\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Wakefield, Mass.) tied the highest balance beam score in EAGL Championship history and was named to the EAGL All-Tournament First Team on beam and Second Team on vault and floor exercise to highlight the UNH gymnastics team's fourth-place finish in the EAGL Championship at the Whittemore Center. Gorgenyi was selected Team MVP following a season in which she earned All-EAGL First Team accolades on uneven bars and Second Team on vault and floor exercise.  She scored a personal-best and school-record-tying 9.950 on bars at Texas Woman's University on Feb. 5. Gorgenyi subsequently earned UNH's Jim Urquhart Student-Athlete of the Year Award,\u003Cspan style=\"font-size:14px;\">given\u003C/span>\u003Cspan style=\"font-size:14px;\"> to the most outstanding senior student-athlete based on athletic success, community involvement and academic achievement through her Wildcat career. \u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2022, the Wildcats set the program's all-time highest score on uneven bars in its Senior Day/Alumni Day quad meet on March 13 before a crowd of 1,660 at the Whittemore Center. UNH's 49.325 bar score eclipsed the previous school record of 49.300 set in 2010. Graduate student co-captain \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=9055\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"9055\">Kylie Kratchwell\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Sewell, N.J.), in her final home meet, and junior \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=9052\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"9052\">Kylie Gorgenyi\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (North Reading, Mass.) headlined the lineup with a 9.900, which equaled Gorgenyi's personal best. \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=9056\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"9056\">Hailey Lui\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Collegeville, Pa.) was named team MVP and was EAGL's regular-season balance beam champion. Lui graduated as a four-time All-EAGL honoree on beam, including three consecutive First-Team berths.The Collegeville, Pa., native competed as an event specialist on beam at the NCAA Regional Championships, hosted by Auburn, and was a finalist for UNH's Jim Urquhart Female Student-Athlete of the Year award.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2021, the Wildcats were ranked No. 35 nationally in the RoadtoNationals.com poll on March 19 when the team had to withdraw from the 2021 EAGL Championship -one day prior to the championship meet at Pitt- due to COVID-19-related protocols. With no ability to compete in that EAGL meet to defend their 2019 championship or add one more score to lock up an NCAA Regional Championship berth, the 'Cats fell out of the Top 36 and finished the season ranked 38\u003Csup>th\u003C/sup> (195.719 National Qualifying Score). Sophomore \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=8322\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"8322\">Robyn Kelley\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Wakefield, Mass.) was named the EAGL Specialist of the Year, the first in school history. Kelly was tabbed team MVP and received the Katie Baldwin Academic Achievement Award to highlight the 2021 UNH gymnastics virtual team awards banquet.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cspan style=\"font-size:14px;\">In 2020, Bruck Ayotte's first season at the helm, the Wildcats earned a share of the inaugural EAGL regular-season championship along with North Carolina State, but UNH was prevented from defending its 2019 EAGL Championship when the season was canceled abruptly March 12 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Seniors \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7646\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"7646\">Riley Freehling\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Southington, Conn.) and \u003Cstrong>\u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7653\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"7653\">Emma Winer\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn>\u003C/strong> (Georgetown, Mass.) were crowned team co-MVPs. The EAGL Championships and NCAA Championships were canceled  due to the COVID-19 public health threat. \u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nBruck Ayotte \u003Cspan style=\"font-size:14px;\">\u003Cspan style=\"font-size:14px;\">was named head coach of the Wildcat women’s gymnastics program July 10, 2019, by Director of Athletics Marty Scarano. Lindsey,\u003C/span>\u003C/span> who served as associate head coach under legendary Gail Goodspeed for three seasons (2017-19), replaced Goodspeed, who retired July 1, 2019, after a 40-year career at the University.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\n\"We are very fortunate to have someone of Lindsey's capability and unique background succeed Gail Goodspeed,” said Scarano. “Gail set a standard that will be difficult to meet, but Lindsey's time spent with UNH prepares her well to do so. Most of all, Lindsey has been a valued member of our UNH family, and she will continue to lead this fabulous program with class.\" \u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\n\"I am extremely honored and excited to be named the next head coach of women’s gymnastics at the University of New Hampshire, and I thank Marty Scarano for this opportunity,” said Bruck Ayotte. “I have been very fortunate to coach this program for over five years and to have used my experience as a Division I gymnast at the University of Michigan and performer/coach at Cirque du Soleil to assist our student-athletes.”\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nAs associate head coach from 2016-19, Bruck Ayotte oversaw all team choreography, handled in-season team travel arrangements, worked alongside Goodspeed in all facets of the training program and was the gymnastics summer camp director. Previously, she was a UNH assistant coach for two seasons (2008-10). The Wildcats reached the NCAA Regional Championships all five seasons that Bruck Ayotte has been on staff.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2019, Bruck Ayotte was named NCAA Northeast Region Assistant Coach of the Year after helping the Wildcats win their third EAGL Championship in program history at the Whittemore Center. She shared the award with assistant coach Sunny Marchand and Datti, the volunteer assistant coach who rides off into the sunset of full-time retirement with Goodspeed, his wife, after 38 years of service to UNH.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nFrom 2008-10, Bruck Ayotte was the Wildcats’ primary choreographer. Her other responsibilities included co-teaching the movement and gymnastics exploration class, overseeing the UNH community gymnastics class program and coordinating the program’s paperwork for numerous aspects. She then left UNH to pursue a life-long dream of performing with Cirque du Soleil and joined a show called Amaluna, where she was an Amazon character. She was captain of the squad, performed a unique uneven-bar act and was promoted to artist coach. She also learned numerous other disciplines and coached contortion, the water bowl act, suspended pole and corde lisse.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nA native of Marietta, N.Y., Bruck Ayotte was a two-time All-American for head coach Bev Plocki at the University of Michigan from 2004-08. She was a Honda Award finalist, 2008 NCAA Woman of the Year nominee and a two-time NCAA Northeast Region Gymnast of the Year. Her other accolades included 2008 Big Ten Gymnast of the Year, three-time All-Big Ten First Team honoree, NACGC/W Academic All-American, ESPN The Magazine Academic All-District First Team and four-time Big Ten All-Academic Team.\u003Cbr style=\"text-align: justify;\">\u003Cstrong>Nick Cramer\u003C/strong> joined the UNH gymnastics program as an assistant coach under seventh-year head coach Lindsey Bruck Ayotte in September 2025, bringing with him a versatile coaching background and extensive experience in both men’s and women’s gymnastics. At UNH, Cramer serves as the primary coach on vault and floor exercise, while also playing a key role in the team’s recruiting efforts\u003Cstrong> \u003C/strong>alongside fellow assistant coach Alyssa Worthington ’23.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\">Cramer also oversees all home meet setup operations at the Whittemore Center at the Key Auto Group Complex and Lundholm Gym, coordinating equipment installation and breakdown to ensure a world-class competition environment for the Wildcats.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\">Before arriving in Durham, Cramer served as program director at Metro Stars Gymnastics, where he led the Junior Olympic boys’ program and managed all elements of athlete development, training plans, and competition coordination. style=\"text-align: justify;\">\u003Cstrong>Alyssa Worthington '23\u003C/strong> joined her alma mater as an assistant coach for Lindsey Bruck Ayotte in August 2024.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2026, her second season on the coaching staff, Alyssa takes on the elevated role of primary choreographer for the balance beam lineup, the lead for home event setup and the primary liaison for the UNH Gymnastics Community Program. Additionally, she has taken on a greater responsibility in recruiting efforts.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2025, Worthington assisted Bruck Ayotte, associate head coach/recruiting coordinator \u003Cstrong>Steve Avgerinos\u003C/strong> and assistant coach \u003Cstrong>Jazmyn Estrella\u003C/strong> in all facets of the program. That included assisting with choreography and the UNH Gymnastics Community Program.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nAlyssa was a three-time NCAA Regional competitor and four-time All-EAGL selection \u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/sports/womens-gymnastics/roster/alyssa-worthington/9486\">during her decorated UNH career\u003C/a>. As a Wildcat from 2020-23, she specialized on balance beam and floor exercise. Her career-high 9.975 on beam (Jan. 23, 2022) is tied for No. 3 all-time in UNH history. style=\"text-align: justify;\">\u003Ca class=\"twitter-follow-button\" href=\"https://twitter.com/FakeMurph595\">Follow @FakeMurph595\u003C/a>\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\">Mike Murphy, now in his 16th year at UNH in 2025-26, was promoted to his current role of Associate Athletic Director for Marketing & Communications on Jan. 28, 2021. In this role, Murphy oversees the communications, marketing and Wildcat Productions teams in support of revenue enhancement, brand strength and visibility. The primary focus of his role is leading the strategy, planning and implementation of an aggressive effort to increase UNH Athletics awareness, driving gameday attendance and overseeing operation of the Athletics Department website, social media accounts and other front-facing content channels.  \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMurphy served as Associate Athletic Director for Communications from Nov. 2013 to Jan. 2021. He managed a team that handled all aspects of the department's day-to-day external relations strategies across multiple platforms, including digital, broadcast and social media. He collaborated with the associate athletic director of marketing and promotions and the associate athletic director of business development in executing the athletic department's core values of enhancing the fan experience, conveying the student-athlete experience, inspiring attendance at athletic events and increasing revenue generation. Further, he worked closely with Wildcat Sports Properties, UNH Athletics' exclusive multimedia rights holder, in both an administrative role and in an on-air capacity as a broadcaster.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMurphy joined the UNH athletic communications staff June 30, 2010, as an Associate Director. He has served as the primary media contact for the Wildcats’ football, gymnastics and skiing programs.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMurphy has led a department that has hosted the NCAA Men's Ice Hockey Regional Championships (2011-13-15-17-19-23), NCAA Ski Championships (2017-21), NCAA Women's Frozen Four (2016-24) and East Atlantic Gymnastics League (EAGL) Championship (2014-19-23).\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMurphy has been part of the Wildcat Sports Radio Network since 1998. He became the radio Voice of UNH Wildcats Hockey in 2016 and subsequently won his sixth (2016), seventh (2017), eighth (2020), ninth (2022) and 10th (2025) New Hampshire Sportscaster of the Year awards from the National Sports Media Association (NSMA). He was previously feted in 1998, 2004, 2006, 2008 and 2009. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMurphy, who hosted the UNH Coaches' Show on the radio for more than a decade, has worked in a TV broadcast capacity as the Voice of UNH Hockey on NESN and ESPN, in addition to serving as Wildcat football color commentator on NBC Sports Boston. Mike has also provided select play-by-play, color commentary and sideline reporting for ESPN3/+ broadcasts for a multitude of Wildcat Athletics events and was the host of the \u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/sports/2020/12/1/unh-wildcast-powered-by-unitil.aspx\">UNHWildCast\u003C/a>, the official podcast of UNH Athletics. He serves as public address announcer for a number of UNH athletics events.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nPreviously, Mike served as the radio color commentator for UNH football games from 1998-2009, men's and women's basketball from 2001-17 and women's hockey from 2008-17. Other past on-air work for UNH Athletics includes hosting the former \u003Ca href=\"http://unhwildcats.com/Inside_Wildcat_Country/index\" style=\"text-align: justify;\" target=\"_blank\">\u003Cem>Inside Wildcat Country\u003C/em>\u003C/a>\u003Cspan style=\"text-align: justify;\">, a television program that offered fans an in-depth look at the inner workings of UNH athletics, \u003C/span> \u003Cspan style=\"text-align: justify;\">on WBIN-TV and Fox College Sports.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHe was named the EAGL co-Administrator of the Year in 2013 when he was the primary athletic communications contact for the eight-team league that included UNH, George Washington, Maryland, North Carolina, North Carolina State, Pittsburgh, Rutgers and Towson.\u003C/span>\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\">Prior to joining the UNH athletic department, Murphy served as the Director of Media Relations and a Ticket Sales Executive for the New Hampshire Fisher Cats, the Toronto Blue Jays’ Double-A affiliate located in Manchester, from 2006-10. In that media relations role, he wrote press releases and game notes, supervised press conferences, served as media liaison and helped maintain the team’s website. He played a significant role as part of the Fisher Cats’ front office that was awarded the prestigious 2009 Double-A Bob Freitas Award by Baseball America in recognition for achieving long-term success in Minor League Baseball.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\">Murphy, honored as the 2008 New Hampshire Association of Broadcasters Air Personality of the Year, was part of the Fisher Cats Radio Network broadcast team from the minor league baseball team's inception in 2004 through 2010. He was also bestowed the A.P. Top Play-by-Play Award in 2001 and 2008 and is a 12-time recipient of the NHAB Golden Mike Award.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\">Murphy joined the Fisher Cats’ front office in a full-time capacity as a Ticket Sales Account Executive in January 2006 following more than a decade of radio experience in the Granite State, where he served as host for the \"Sports Zone\" talk show on 107.7, the Pulse, and on WKXL radio in Concord.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\">Murphy is a graduate of Syracuse University, where he earned a degree in Broadcast Journalism in 1995.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\">Mike married his wife, Tish, in May 1995. They live in Concord with their son, Jason. Their daughter Katarina Murphy Doucette is a 2019 UNH graduate with a Hospitality Management Degree from the Peter T. She has also overseen several America East and EAGL gymnastics conference playoffs and championships.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\">Prior to UNH, Kimball spent four years as the Assistant Track and Field Coach at the University of Rhode Island.
